history.dynasty: Pallava (enlarged by the Cholas; rebuilt by the Vijayanagara kings)
history.period: 8th century CE (a grant edict is dated 808 CE, by Pallava king Nandi Varman)
history.summary: The Arulmigu Sri Parthasarathy Swamy Temple at Triplicane (Thiruvallikkeni) is the oldest religious structure in Chennai and one of the 108 Divya Desams, the holy abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alwars. Tradition attributes its foundation to the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I in the 8th century; one tradition credits the Chola king Sumati Raja, who longed to see Venkateswara as Krishna, and says the sage Athreya Maharshi installed the idol. Inscriptions on the temple walls record grants from Vijayanagara kings. The presiding deity is Krishna as Parthasarathi, Arjuna's charioteer in the Kurukshetra war - unique in several ways: he carries only the conch and not the discus, honouring his vow to remain unarmed; he wears a prominent moustache marking him as a charioteer; and the utsava deity even bears pit-marks said to be arrow wounds from the battle. Uniquely, Krishna is worshipped together with his family in the sanctum - Rukmini on his right, Satyaki on his left, Balarama facing north to Rukmini's right, and Pradyumna and Aniruddha facing south. The complex holds separate shrines for Narasimha, Rama, Varaha, Ranganatha, Gajendra Varadharaja, Vedavalli Thayar, Andal, Anjaneya, the Alwars, Ramanuja and Vedanta Desika, with the Kairavini Pushkarini tank nearby. The temple is administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department.

name: Parthasarathy Temple
town: Triplicane (CSV town 'Chennai' - the temple is in the Triplicane/Thiruvallikkeni neighbourhood of Chennai city)
town_description: Triplicane (Tamil: Thiruvallikkeni, 'the holy lily pond') is one of Chennai's oldest neighbourhoods, a dense, walkable quarter of agraharam lanes and heritage homes just south of the city centre, adjoining Marina Beach. It is Chennai's Vaishnavite heartland, dominated by the Parthasarathy Temple, and doubles as the city's cultural-intellectual quarter - home to Carnatic musicians, writers and old eateries. The area is well served by the MRTS (Thiruvallikeni station), MTC buses and autos.
tradition: Hindu (Vaishnavism - one of the 108 Divya Desams)

visitor_information.best_time: November to February, when Chennai's weather is coolest; plan February-March for the flower festival (Vasantotsavam). Vaikuntha Ekadasi (December-January) and the Chithirai Brahmotsavam (April-May) are the grandest festivals but draw huge crowds.
